name: Beauty · Randa Rosa style
description: Behaviours her beauty, nails and comedy videos are about, plus four catchphrases reported for her (pookie, 'your next opponent is you', 'you already know the drill', 'my flight leaves in … hours'). The catchphrases are unverified: watch a video with this set and see which actually fire. Examples are illustrative lines, not quotes.

detectors.name: Makeup and beauty talk
detectors.what: the speaker talks about makeup, skincare, lashes or a beauty routine
detectors.example: First I'm doing my lashes, then a little highlighter.

detectors.name: Nail talk
detectors.what: the speaker talks about nails: their length, shape, polish, nail art or the salon
detectors.example: These nails are so long I can barely hold my phone.

detectors.name: Long-nail struggle
detectors.what: the speaker describes a comic difficulty doing an ordinary task because of very long nails
detectors.example: Opening a soda can with these nails is basically impossible.

detectors.name: Glow-up or reveal
detectors.what: the speaker describes a before-and-after change or reveals a finished look
detectors.example: And now the big reveal: from long blue to black stiletto.

detectors.name: Product or tool mention
detectors.what: the speaker names a product, brand, tool or supply they are using
detectors.example: I'm using this gel polish and the little UV lamp.

detectors.name: Budget tip
detectors.what: the speaker mentions a price, saving money or a cheaper alternative
detectors.example: This whole set was under twenty dollars.

detectors.name: Tutorial steps
detectors.what: the speaker explains how to do something step by step
detectors.example: First file the edges, then add the base coat.

detectors.name: Challenge or time limit
detectors.what: the speaker sets a challenge or a time limit for what they are doing
detectors.example: I have fifteen minutes to finish this whole look.

detectors.name: Chaotic mishap
detectors.what: the speaker describes something going wrong or an accident, in a funny way
detectors.example: And of course I just smudged everything.

detectors.name: Hype and compliments
detectors.what: the speaker hypes up or compliments themselves or the viewers
detectors.example: You look so pretty, go get them.

detectors.name: Everyday task
detectors.what: the speaker describes doing an ordinary daily task such as cooking, driving or shopping
detectors.example: Now I'm just trying to make some toast.

detectors.name: Talks to viewers
detectors.what: the speaker addresses the audience directly with a greeting, a sign-off or a call to action
detectors.example: Cheers for watching, and don't forget to subscribe.

detectors.name: “Pookie” (reported)
detectors.what: the speaker calls the audience or someone else "pookie" or "pookies"
detectors.example: Hey pookies, welcome back to the channel.

detectors.name: “Your next opponent is you” (reported)
detectors.what: the speaker tells the audience, as encouragement, that their real competition is themselves
detectors.example: Remember, your next opponent is you.

detectors.name: “You already know the drill” (reported)
detectors.what: the speaker says, in a playful sassy way, that the audience already knows what is going on or what to do

detectors.name: “My flight leaves in … hours” (reported)
detectors.what: the speaker says a flight leaves in a number of hours or that they are about to travel
detectors.example: My flight leaves in three hours.
